lines: Hosts a 64-bit VST 2 or VST 3 instrument inside Rack: pitch and gate become MIDI notes, 16 of the plugin's parameters take CV, and its audio comes back out
0V to 10V over the VST parameter mapped to it. Click its label and move a knob or slider in the plugin's editor to map one, or right-click the label to pick from a list
1V/oct pitch, rounded to the nearest note as the gate rises. A polyphonic cable here plays the plugin polyphonically
A rise here starts a MIDI note at the pitch on the CV input, and the note is held until this falls to 0V
Left channel of the audio the plugin produces
Right channel of the audio the plugin produces
Note — click the plugin name to choose from the VST plugins installed, and the eye beside it reopens the plugin's editor window
Note — the plugin menu also adds and removes the directories searched for VST plugins. The search is recursive and runs at once, with no need to restart Rack
Note — many VST plugins are not built for fast parameter changes, so audio-rate modulation into a parameter input can misbehave, run heavy on CPU or crash the plugin
Menu — block size is how many samples are gathered before the plugin is asked to process them: 128 by default, which is 2.9ms at 44.1kHz, 16 at the least and 4096 at the most

Hosts a 64-bit VST 2 or VST 3 plugin with eight audio inputs, eight audio outputs and 24 parameters taking CV. An instrument plugin is played through its MIDI parameters instead

Audio into the plugin's first channel; with no cable in 2/R this signal feeds that channel too
Audio into the plugin's second channel; with no cable here the first channel's signal is used
Audio into that channel of the plugin
Audio out of that channel of the plugin

Turns MIDI generated by a hosted VST plugin into pitch, gates and clocks. It goes immediately to the right of a Host, Host-FX or Host-XL and takes the MIDI that module's plugin sends
1V/oct pitch of the last note held
10V while a note is held; notes played legato do not restart it
Velocity of the note, 0V to 10V
Aftertouch, which is channel pressure rather than pressure per note
Pitch wheel, -5V to +5V
Mod wheel as a voltage
A clock pulse for every 24-PPQN MIDI clock that arrives
A clock at the division chosen by CLK/N rate in the menu
A trigger when the plugin sends a MIDI start event
A trigger when the plugin sends a MIDI stop event
A trigger when the plugin sends a MIDI continue event
A trigger for every new note, legato or not
Note — click the display to take a single MIDI channel from the plugin instead of all of them
Note — these MIDI expanders can be chained, each one passing MIDI on to the module at its right
Menu — polyphony sets how many channels the outputs carry, and how notes are handed to them: rotate, reuse or reset
Turns MIDI CC messages generated by a hosted VST plugin into CV. It goes immediately to the right of a Host, Host-FX or Host-XL and takes the MIDI that module's plugin sends
The CC assigned to it, 0 to 127 mapped to 0V to 10V. Click its number in the display, then type a CC number or move a control to learn one

Turns MIDI notes generated by a hosted VST plugin into gates. It goes immediately to the right of a Host, Host-FX or Host-XL and takes the MIDI that module's plugin sends
10V while the note assigned to it is held, or a 1ms trigger when note on and note off arrive together. Click its note in the display to change which note it answers
